title: The Carbonyl Group: Structure and Polarity
subject: Chemistry
objective: Why the carbon of C=O is every nucleophile's target: an sp², planar carbon, a π bond from sideways p–p overlap, and a polar C=O with δ⁺ carbon and δ⁻ oxygen, explained by resonance.

fill.q: The bond angles around the carbonyl carbon are about ____ degrees.
In C=O, the oxygen carries a partial ____ charge.
The π bond of C=O forms by sideways overlap of ____ orbitals.

tf.explain: The carbon and the three atoms on it lie in one plane.
The oxygen is δ⁻ and nucleophilic; the carbon is electrophilic.

tf.q: Carbonyl compounds are more polar than ethers.

ar.r: Oxygen pulls the C=O electrons towards itself.
The carbonyl carbon is sp² hybridised.

mcq.q: The carbonyl carbon forms how many σ bonds?
mcq.explain: sp² carbon: three σ bonds and one π bond.

mcq.q: The dipolar resonance structure of C=O is:
mcq.explain: The π electrons move onto oxygen.

num.q: How many lone pairs does the carbonyl oxygen carry?

short.q: Why do nucleophiles attack the carbon of a carbonyl group?
short.solution: Oxygen is more electronegative, so the carbon is δ⁺ (electron-poor, electrophilic); the dipolar resonance structure C⁺–O⁻ shows it too.

match.explain: Each feature matches what it gives the carbonyl group.
